children: Technology companies in Telangana raised $726 million in equity funding in the first nine months of 2026, which is more than three times the $199 million they raised in the same period last year. The ten largest rounds accounted for $664 million, or 91 per cent of the total, according to data intelligence platform Tracxn Technologies Limited.

The number of funding rounds fell 30 per cent to 73 from 105, while the average round size rose to $9.9 million from $1.9 million, Tracxn said in a report released on Friday. Funding was 12 per cent higher than the $647 million raised in the first nine months of 2024.

Hyderabad-based data centre company CtrlS raised $423 million in June in a Series B round backed by CPP Investments. The largest round of the period, it accounted for 58 per cent of all funding. CtrlS raised $451 million in all, including $28.2 million in a Series A round in February.
Skyroot Aerospace, which makes launch vehicles for small satellites, raised $60 million in a Series C round in May.

“Skyroot becoming a unicorn and CtrlS raising one of the year’s largest rounds show that Hyderabad is now building globally relevant infrastructure companies, not just services,” M Srinivasa Rao, former CEO of T-Hub, said.

Seed funding fell 35 per cent to $26.4 million, with 50 rounds against 77 a year earlier. Across all stages, 20 companies raised funds for the first time, down from 29. Rao said more capital needed to reach seed-stage founders and first-time entrepreneurs.

Late-stage funding rose to $78.1 million across four rounds, from $14.8 million across two. The number of active investors fell 22 per cent to 61 from 78. Tracxn counted 13 international investors, down from 23, and 30 first-time investors, down from 47.

By sector, enterprise infrastructure companies raised $454 million, up from $13 million a year earlier. They accounted for 63 per cent of all funding. Enterprise applications came next with $142 million, up 79 per cent from $79.4 million. Funding for aerospace, maritime and defence technology companies rose 445 per cent to $78.5 million from $14.4 million.

Serial entrepreneur and investor Aditya Vuchi said CtrlS and Skyroot accounted for much of the capital raised. Attributing funding to a city was “a bit more nuanced,” he said, as some companies that raised between $5 million and $20 million might have their headquarters elsewhere. The number of Hyderabad-based funds had also risen, though some might invest outside the city, he said.

Acquisitions fell to six from nine a year earlier. Emami acquired IncNut Digital for $33.9 million in May, the only acquisition with a disclosed price. Hyderabad-based DSPL was the only company to go public. It listed in January at a market cap of $32.9 million.

title: Telangana tech firms raise $726 million in first nine months of 2026
